lessons.name: Air Street Capital
lessons.summary: Air Street Capital is a London venture capital firm that invests very early in AI-first companies, including robot-learning startups such as Sereact.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Air Street Capital is a London venture capital firm that invests very early in AI-first companies, including robot-learning startups such as Sereact.

![State of AI Report 2026 title card by Nathan Benaich and Air Street Capital](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-air-street-capital.webp)
*State of AI Report 2026 title card by Nathan Benaich and Air Street Capital. Source: [Air Street Press](https://press.airstreet.com/p/state-of-ai-2026), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Early AI bets:** Air Street invests "as early as possible" in AI-first companies across North America and Europe, and announced a $232M Fund III.
- **Sereact backer:** It was a returning investor in Sereact's $110M Series B (April 2026). Sereact sells Cortex, a robot "brain" model for picking and assembly.
- **State of AI Report:** Founder Nathan Benaich publishes this yearly report; the 2026 edition is the 9th and runs to 244 slides.
- **Robotics thesis:** The 2026 essay argues robotics is approaching its "GPT-2 moment" as models, hardware and data collection come together.

> **Key idea:** Air Street's free report is the fastest way to see how investors read robot-learning research.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Reading list:** The report's robotics slides summarise the year's world models and robot foundation models in one place.
- **Thesis check:** Our wedge (robot learning on low-cost arms) matches the category Air Street funds, so their essays test whether it is credible.

## How to engage

1. **Read the State of AI Report** robotics section and list three claims you could test on an SO-101.
2. **Subscribe to Air Street Press** for the monthly State of AI newsletter and essays.
3. **Watch RAAIS talks**, the summit where Benaich presents each report.
4. **Write a short public post** reacting to a report prediction, and share it with the authors.

lessons.name: Amadeus Capital Partners
lessons.summary: Amadeus Capital Partners is a Cambridge and London deep-tech venture firm that has recently led early rounds in robot-planning and warehouse-robot startups.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Amadeus Capital Partners is a Cambridge and London deep-tech venture firm that has recently led early rounds in robot-planning and warehouse-robot startups.

![Collaborative robot arm working in a warehouse shelving system at NEOintralogistics](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-amadeus-capital-partners.webp)
*Collaborative robot arm working in a warehouse shelving system at NEOintralogistics. Source: [Amadeus Capital Partners](https://www.amadeuscapital.com/neointralogistics-e3m-raas-warehouse-automation/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Deep-tech since 1997:** Founded by Anne Glover and Hermann Hauser, Amadeus has backed more than 200 companies and raised over $1.3 billion.
- **Stateful Robotics:** In March 2026 it co-led a $4.8M pre-seed for this Oxford spin-out, which gives robots a persistent memory of tasks and sites.
- **NEOintralogistics:** In January 2026 its APEX fund co-led a €3M seed for this Düsseldorf **robots-as-a-service** (RaaS: rent, don't buy) warehouse-picking startup.

> **Key idea:** Robots that remember past failures can replan when an aisle is blocked, and investors now fund that layer.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software angle:** Stateful Robotics is a software layer for long missions, close to what a software-heavy team can build.
- **Business models:** NEOintralogistics shows RaaS, where customers rent robots and pay little upfront.
- **Mentor contact:** A UK firm with repeated robotics deals is a credible speaker on how early robot startups get funded.

## How to engage

1. **Read the two deal announcements** and note the problem each startup claims to solve.
2. **Subscribe to Capitalise**, the Amadeus newsletter on deep-tech companies.
3. **Listen to Hermann Hauser** on how deep-tech companies start.
4. **Use "Submit a proposal"** only for a real company, not for a student club request.

lessons.name: Atomico
lessons.summary: Atomico is a London venture capital firm, founded by entrepreneurs, that backs Dexory and publishes research on deploying robots across Europe.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Atomico is a London venture capital firm, founded by entrepreneurs, that backs Dexory and publishes research on deploying robots across Europe.

![Autonomous warehouse-scanning robot between tall pallet racks, from Atomico's The Great Rollout](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-atomico.webp)
*Autonomous warehouse-scanning robot between tall pallet racks, from Atomico's The Great Rollout. Source: [Atomico](https://atomico.com/insights/the-great-rollout), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Founder-built VC:** Atomico calls itself "the founder-built European venture capital firm" and invests at venture and growth stage.
- **Dexory investor:** It is an existing investor in Dexory, whose autonomous robots scan warehouses and feed a **digital twin** (a live software copy of the building).
- **The Great Rollout:** Its 2026 essay argues the hard problem moved from building robots to deploying them at scale and collecting their data.

> **Key idea:** In Atomico's view, value now forms in deployment and data loops, not in the robot body.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Market map:** The essay walks through the robotics stack: hardware, hands, software, data and deployment.
- **Concrete numbers:** It notes some robot bodies fell from hundreds of thousands of dollars a decade ago to tens of thousands today.
- **Data mindset:** Dexory has logged more than a billion warehouse location scans, a real-world example of the data flywheel our lab talks about.

## How to engage

1. **Read The Great Rollout** and mark which stack layer each 42AI project targets.
2. **Watch Atomico's chat with Dexory** to hear how a robot startup scales.
3. **Read the State of European Tech** report for the wider funding picture.
4. **Share a project write-up** with Atomico's team on public channels if it addresses deployment or data.

lessons.name: Bpifrance
lessons.summary: Bpifrance is France's public investment bank, which funds French startups, including industrial robot companies such as Galam Robotics, through loans, grants and equity.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Bpifrance is France's public investment bank, which funds French startups, including industrial robot companies such as Galam Robotics, through loans, grants and equity.

![Galam Robotics TAK-ONE automated storage system in a logistics hall](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-bpifrance.webp)
*Galam Robotics TAK-ONE automated storage system in a logistics hall. Source: [Supernova Invest](https://supernovainvest.com/supporting-galam-robotics-with-e10m-to-revolutionize-automated-logistics-market/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Plan Tech:** Bpifrance's tech plan aims to fund innovation, "accelerate deeptech" from first idea to scale, and grow tomorrow's tech champions.
- **Industrial seed funds:** In November 2026 it launched **Bpifrance Amorçage Industriel 2**, a €75M fund, bringing its equity for industrial startups to €125M.
- **Galam Robotics:** Its industrial seed fund joined a €10M round for Galam, whose TAK-ONE storage system slides bins like a sliding puzzle.
- **Calls for projects:** It runs public competitions and calls (*appels à projets*) that startups apply to for funding.

> **Key idea:** For a French robot startup, Bpifrance is often the first public money: grants and loans before or beside VCs.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Home ecosystem:** We are in Paris, so Bpifrance programmes are the ones a future 42AI spin-off could actually apply to.
- **Event stage:** It publishes talks on humanoid robotics and deep tech, useful for learning how French investors see the field.
- **Vocabulary:** Its pages teach funding words (seed, equity, deeptech) every founder must know.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Bpifrance's humanoid-robotics talk** (in French) for the investor view.
2. **Read the Plan Tech page** and note which tools fit a student team.
3. **Browse open calls for projects** to see what a funded robotics project must show.
4. **Attend Bpifrance Inno Generation (BIG)** or other public Bpifrance events to meet founders.

lessons.name: Cathay Innovation
lessons.summary: Cathay Innovation is a global venture capital firm with a Paris base that names robotics as a focus area and backed Barcelona robot maker THEKER.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Cathay Innovation is a global venture capital firm with a Paris base that names robotics as a focus area and backed Barcelona robot maker THEKER.

![THEKER $85M Series A announcement card from Cathay Innovation](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-cathay-innovation.webp)
*THEKER $85M Series A announcement card from Cathay Innovation. Source: [Cathay Capital](https://www.cathaycapital.com/theker-raises-85m-in-europes-largest-ever-robotics-series-a-led-by-crv-with-backing-from-samsung-and-lvmh/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Robotics focus area:** Its "AI-Driven Robotics" page says "the next revolution is physical", covering operating rooms, factory floors and connected devices.
- **THEKER:** Cathay joined THEKER's $85M Series A (June 2026), led by CRV and called Europe's largest robotics Series A. THEKER builds **generalist robots** for factories.
- **Corporate network:** Its $1B fund closed in 2025 with more than 20 international corporations behind it, such as industrial partners Valeo and Air Liquide.

> **Key idea:** A corporate-backed VC can link a robot startup to factories that become its first customers.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Generalist robots:** THEKER aims for one AI-native robot that handles many factory tasks, the same goal as robot learning on low-cost arms.
- **European focus:** Its $1B fund is pitched as powering Europe's industry transformation, where factory robots fit.
- **Investor writing:** Its essays, such as "The Industrialization of Embodied Robotic Intelligence", explain the market in plain language.

## How to engage

1. **Read the Robotics / IoT page** and its "Behind the Term Sheet: Theker" story.
2. **Watch THEKER's co-founder** explain generalist factory robots.
3. **Follow Cathay's News & Insights** for robotics essays.
4. **Invite a Cathay speaker** to a 42AI demo day once we have a working project.

lessons.name: Creandum
lessons.summary: Creandum is a European early-stage venture firm that led big robot-learning rounds for Sereact in Germany and Machenta in London.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Creandum is a European early-stage venture firm that led big robot-learning rounds for Sereact in Germany and Machenta in London.

![The Machenta founding team, an Imperial College London robot-learning spin-out](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-creandum.webp)
*The Machenta founding team, an Imperial College London robot-learning spin-out. Source: [Imperial College London](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/articles/2026/imperial-ai-spinout-machenta-raises-40-million-to-make-robots-instant-learners/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Early backer:** Creandum's motto is backing "the companies of tomorrow before it's obvious", mostly at seed and Series A.
- **Sereact:** It led Sereact's €25M Series A in January 2025 and returned in the $110M Series B. Sereact's AI lets robots pick and handle items.
- **Machenta:** In October 2026 it co-led, with Union Square Ventures, Machenta's $40M seed, the largest seed ever raised by a UK robotics startup.

> **Key idea:** Machenta's pitch is **one-shot learning**: a robot learns a new task from a single human demonstration, not hundreds.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Thesis match:** Both deals are robot-learning companies, the exact wedge 42AI wants to test with imitation learning.
- **Research to startup:** Machenta grew from Edward Johns's robot-learning research at Imperial, a model for lab-to-company paths.
- **Benchmark:** Sereact's picking demo shows what "good enough for customers" looks like.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Sereact's picking demo** and note what an SO-101 project would need to match.
2. **Read Imperial's Machenta article** to learn why demonstrations are costly today.
3. **Follow Creandum's Stories** for founder interviews.
4. **Share a public demo video** that shows learning from few demonstrations.

lessons.name: DCVC
lessons.summary: DCVC is a US deep-tech venture firm that has backed humanoid-robot maker Agility Robotics since 2020 and writes about robots in warehouses.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

DCVC is a US deep-tech venture firm that has backed humanoid-robot maker Agility Robotics since 2020 and writes about robots in warehouses.

![Agility Robotics Digit humanoids carrying totes beside warehouse shelving](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-dcvc.webp)
*Agility Robotics Digit humanoids carrying totes beside warehouse shelving. Source: [DCVC](https://www.dcvc.com/companies/agility-robotics/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Agility since 2020:** DCVC lists 2020 as its first investment in Agility Robotics and co-led that round.
- **Warehouse humanoids:** Agility's Digit picks up and carries totes, stacks boxes and loads trailers in spaces built for people.
- **Deep Tech Opportunities report:** DCVC's yearly report covers physical AI; the 2025 edition argues "robots should be backward-compatible with the real world".

> **Key idea:** A humanoid's selling point is fitting existing buildings, so no one rebuilds the warehouse around the robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Design lesson:** "Backward-compatible" robots work in human spaces, a useful test for any project we pitch.
- **Data lesson:** DCVC calls Agility "a real-world case study in operational data", the same loop as robot learning.
- **US view:** It contrasts with our mostly European investor list.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Digit's first day at GXO** to see a humanoid in a real warehouse job.
2. **Read DCVC's Agility page** and its linked Deep Tech Opportunities chapters.
3. **Watch DCVC's SOSV talk** on how a deep-tech fund thinks.
4. **Quote their reports** in project write-ups; contact them only through public channels.

lessons.name: EBRD Venture Capital
lessons.summary: EBRD Venture Capital is the startup-investing arm of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which led the $44M Series B of Polish picking-robot maker Nomagic.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

EBRD Venture Capital is the startup-investing arm of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which led the $44M Series B of Polish picking-robot maker Nomagic.

![Nomagic robot arm picking items from blue totes in a warehouse cell](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-ebrd-venture-capital.webp)
*Nomagic robot arm picking items from blue totes in a warehouse cell. Source: [EBRD](https://www.ebrd.com/home/news-and-events/news/2025/ebrd-invests-in-polish-based-robotics-company-nomagic.html), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Development-bank VC:** The **EBRD** is a multilateral bank that invests in businesses in its regions; its venture team funds technology startups.
- **Nomagic lead:** It led Nomagic's $44M (€41.9M) Series B, with Khosla Ventures and Almaz Capital co-investing.
- **What Nomagic does:** Its AI robot arms pick, pack and sort goods for e-commerce, working 24/7 with little oversight under a robot-as-a-service model.

> **Key idea:** **Piece picking** (grabbing one item from a messy bin) is hard because every object differs, so AI vision matters.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Picking problem:** Nomagic says its justPick system does up to 500 picks per hour, a clear benchmark for a manipulation project.
- **Central Europe:** EBRD backs companies outside the usual Paris-London-Berlin hubs, widening our map.
- **VLMs in robots:** The EBRD release says Nomagic uses vision language models, linking software AI skills to real arms.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Nomagic robots at Arvato** to see piece picking in a real warehouse.
2. **Read the EBRD announcement** and The Robot Report article side by side.
3. **Try a pick-and-place task** on an SO-101 with varied objects.
4. **Follow EBRD's news page** for later robotics deals.

lessons.name: EIC Fund (European Innovation Council)
lessons.summary: The EIC Fund is the European Commission's venture capital arm, investing in deep-tech startups such as robotic concrete-factory maker Hyperion Robotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The EIC Fund is the European Commission's venture capital arm, investing in deep-tech startups such as robotic concrete-factory maker Hyperion Robotics.

![Hyperion Robotics' Forge I robotic factory building at night](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-eic-fund.webp)
*Hyperion Robotics' Forge I robotic factory building at night. Source: [The Engineer](https://www.theengineer.co.uk/content/news/hyperion-raises-74m-for-robotic-concrete-factories), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **EU venture arm:** Set up in 2020, the EIC Fund invests for the **European Innovation Council**, with over €4 billion, from seed to Series B.
- **Hyperion Robotics:** It co-led a $7.4M round for this Finnish company, whose robotic microfactories 3D-print low-carbon concrete foundations.
- **Accelerator link:** The wider EIC Accelerator gives grants plus equity; Nanoflex Robotics received €12.5M to steer medical guidewires with magnets.

> **Key idea:** EU money comes as "blended finance": a grant plus an equity stake, so one award can fund both research and growth.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Scale signal:** The EIC says it backs 300+ companies in 25 countries, so many European robot startups pass through it.
- **Applied robotics:** Hyperion uses Forge, a software platform linking design, engineering and robots, which shows where software developers fit.
- **Future funding:** A deep-tech spin-off from our lab would likely meet EIC programmes.

## How to engage

1. **Read the EIC Fund page** to learn the vocabulary (equity, blended finance, Series B).
2. **Watch Michiel Scheffer** explain how the EIC works with VCs.
3. **Read the Hyperion and Nanoflex stories** for two very different robots.
4. **Follow the EIC news pages** for new robotics awards and investments.

lessons.name: Elaia
lessons.summary: Elaia is a Paris deep-tech venture firm that led the $16M seed of Zurich robot-hand startup mimic and also backs warehouse-robot company Dexory.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Elaia is a Paris deep-tech venture firm that led the $16M seed of Zurich robot-hand startup mimic and also backs warehouse-robot company Dexory.

![Elaia logo](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-elaia.webp)
*Elaia logo. Source: [Elaia](https://elaia.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Full-stack investor:** Elaia invests from pre-seed to pre-IPO and often starts "when innovation is still taking shape in labs".
- **Mimic seed:** It led mimic's oversubscribed $16M seed. mimic, a 2024 ETH Zurich spin-off, builds humanoid robot hands and foundation AI models.
- **Fund V:** Its Digital Venture Fund V had a €120M first close in 2026, with €1M–€15M tickets; its first investment was mimic.
- **Dexory:** Elaia is also an existing investor in warehouse-scanning robot maker Dexory.

> **Key idea:** mimic solves robotics' data shortage by having factory workers wear data-collection devices, then training robots by **imitation learning**.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Same method:** Imitation learning from human demonstrations is our lab's core hypothesis, and mimic does it commercially.
- **Paris investor:** Elaia is in Paris, so its partners can attend local events.
- **Lab-to-startup:** Its pre-seed focus suits research-born teams like a future 42AI spin-off.

## How to engage

1. **Watch "Meet mimic"** from Elaia's channel.
2. **Read the mimic seed article** and list the data-collection steps.
3. **Record your own demonstrations** with LeRobot and compare the workflow.
4. **Follow Elaia's news** for robotics deals.

lessons.name: ETH Pioneer Fellowship
lessons.summary: The ETH Pioneer Fellowship is ETH Zurich's incubation programme that funds and coaches students and researchers turning their research into spin-offs, including robotics companies like ANYbotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The ETH Pioneer Fellowship is ETH Zurich's incubation programme that funds and coaches students and researchers turning their research into spin-offs, including robotics companies like ANYbotics.

![Marco Hutter, ANYbotics co-founder and former Pioneer Fellow, beside a robot in his ETH lab](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-eth-pioneer-fellowship.webp)
*Marco Hutter, ANYbotics co-founder and former Pioneer Fellow, beside a robot in his ETH lab. Source: [ETH Foundation](https://ethz-foundation.ch/en/spotlight/uplift-13-robotics-on-the-rise/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research to company:** Fellows get funding, coaching and 12–18 months of support to turn ETH research into a market-ready **spin-off** (a company born from a lab).
- **Money and help:** Deep-Tech fellows receive CHF 120,000 for 12 months in engineering fields, plus a host professor and ETH infrastructure.
- **Robotics alumni:** Marco Hutter was a Pioneer Fellow on his way to founding ANYbotics; the ETH Foundation also lists Tethys Robotics, Caterra, Scewo and Gravis Robotics.

> **Key idea:** A fellowship pays a researcher to test whether a lab robot can become a product, before any investor arrives.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Proven pipeline:** It links ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab (RSL) research to companies such as ANYbotics and Gravis Robotics.
- **Model to copy:** Its steps (prototype, coaching, market test) are a template for our 4–6 month lab.
- **Eligibility:** It is only for ETH students and researchers, so 42AI members cannot apply directly.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 15-year anniversary video** to see the range of fellow projects.
2. **Read "Robotics on the rise"** and look up two of the robot startups.
3. **Read the programme page** for the phases a deep-tech project goes through.
4. **Ask programme staff** for a robotics alumni speaker for a 42AI event.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Eurazeo is a listed investment group whose growth team led the £75M Series C of Dexory, a London maker of warehouse-scanning robots.

![Dexory team in front of its tall autonomous scanning robots in a warehouse](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-eurazeo.webp)
*Dexory team in front of its tall autonomous scanning robots in a warehouse. Source: [British Business Bank](https://www.british-business-bank.co.uk/news-and-events/news/british-business-bank-invests-ps85-million-dexory), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Private markets group:** Eurazeo describes itself as a major player in private-markets asset management, with venture, growth and debt teams.
- **Dexory Series C:** Its Growth team led Dexory's £75M Series C in October 2025, part of a £124M raise, with Atomico and Elaia among existing backers.
- **What Dexory does:** Tall autonomous robots drive aisles scanning shelves, and the AI DexoryView platform turns scans into a **digital twin** of the warehouse.

> **Key idea:** Growth investors fund robots that already have customers; Dexory lists GXO, Maersk, DHL and Stellantis.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Later stage:** Eurazeo shows what investors expect after the seed stage: real deployments and revenue.
- **Software value:** Dexory's product is as much data platform as robot, a natural fit for software students.
- **Scale stories:** Dexory recently opened a North American headquarters in Nashville, a case study in taking robots abroad.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Dexory's robot video** to see autonomous warehouse scanning.
2. **Read the BusinessCloud article** for Dexory's customers and growth since 2024.
3. **Watch Romain Mombert of Eurazeo Growth** talk about growth investing.
4. **Follow Eurazeo's news feed** for new deep-tech deals.

lessons.name: FINOVAM Gestion
lessons.summary: FINOVAM Gestion is a French technology investor whose portfolio includes the painting-robot startup Les Companions and exoskeleton maker Japet.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FINOVAM Gestion is a French technology investor whose portfolio includes the painting-robot startup Les Companions and exoskeleton maker Japet.

![Les Companions logo, robots for painters](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-finovam-gestion.webp)
*Les Companions logo, robots for painters. Source: [FINOVAM Gestion](https://finovamgestion.fr/portfolio/les-companions/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Tech investor:** FINOVAM says it invests in "future technology leaders", in IT, bio-economy, health and the **industry of the future**.
- **Les Companions:** A robotics startup from research at École des Mines et Télécoms de Lille. Its first robot paints interior walls and ceilings, the most tiring tasks.
- **Japet:** A French medical-device company whose product Atlas is an **exoskeleton** (a wearable powered frame) that relieves back pain at work.

> **Key idea:** Investors like FINOVAM back robots that remove painful work, such as ceiling painting or heavy lifting.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Service robots:** Both companies solve one concrete human task, a good scope for a student project.
- **Lab to startup:** Les Companions grew from research at a Lille engineering school, a path a 42AI project could follow.
- **Unknowns:** Current fund size and investment terms are not stated on the pages we opened.

## How to engage

1. **Watch PACO, the painting robot** from Les Companions.
2. **Read the two portfolio pages** and note which part of each robot is software.
3. **Watch the Université de Lille clip** with a FINOVAM speaker.
4. **Use the official contact form** to ask for a founder introduction, not funding.

lessons.name: Founderful
lessons.summary: Founderful is a Zurich venture firm, formerly Wingman Ventures, that leads first funding rounds for Swiss startups, including drone maker Wingtra and robot-hand startup mimic.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Founderful is a Zurich venture firm, formerly Wingman Ventures, that leads first funding rounds for Swiss startups, including drone maker Wingtra and robot-hand startup mimic.

![mimic robot hand performing an assembly task](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-founderful.webp)
*mimic robot hand performing an assembly task. Source: [startupticker.ch](https://www.startupticker.ch/en/news/mimic-robotics-banks-16-million-seed-funding), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **First investor:** Founderful backs Swiss founder teams as **lead investor** in their first financing round: "first, fast, and founder-friendly".
- **Robotics focus:** Startupticker says it supports B2B software and industrial tech, from robotics and industrial automation to computer vision.
- **Portfolio:** It has backed over 50 startups, including survey-drone maker Wingtra, and joined mimic's $16M seed round led by Elaia.
- **Fund II:** Renamed from Wingman Ventures, it announced $85M at first close of a $120M target.

> **Key idea:** A pre-seed lead investor bets on a team and a prototype, often before any customer exists.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Lab-born teams:** mimic is a 2024 ETH Zurich spin-off, so Founderful backs robotics teams straight out of labs.
- **Founder view:** Its partners were founders themselves, so talks focus on starting a company.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Wingtra's drone video** to see a Founderful portfolio robot.
2. **Read the Founderful name-change article** for its focus areas.
3. **Watch the IMD episode** with Founderful's Edouard Treccani.
4. **Request a short talk** on commercialising robotics, not investment.

lessons.name: FuturePlay
lessons.summary: FuturePlay is a Seoul deep-tech venture firm that funds and helps build early startups, including WIRobotics, maker of wearable walking robots and the ALLEX humanoid.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FuturePlay is a Seoul deep-tech venture firm that funds and helps build early startups, including WIRobotics, maker of wearable walking robots and the ALLEX humanoid.

![WIRobotics' ALLEX humanoid robot, developed for human-level manipulation](/img/lessons/orgs_investor_1-futureplay.webp)
*WIRobotics' ALLEX humanoid robot, developed for human-level manipulation. Source: [WIRobotics](https://www.wirobotics.com/media/newsDetail?idx=177), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Company builder:** FuturePlay calls itself deep-tech venture capital for "full-cycle startup growth": early funding, help building teams and support finding later investors.
- **WIRobotics:** Its portfolio includes WIRobotics, and in May 2026 FuturePlay joined WIRobotics' 95 billion won (950억 원) Series B, led by JB Investment.
- **Wearable to humanoid:** WIRobotics first sold WIM, a walking-assist wearable robot, and reuses about three years of user data to build ALLEX.

> **Key idea:** WIRobotics reuses motion data and control code from a simpler product to build a harder robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Asian view:** It adds a Korean deep-tech investor to a mostly European map.
- **Product path:** Starting with a narrow product before a humanoid is a realistic strategy for a small team.
- **Wearables:** WIM shows robotics also means wearable devices, not only arms and wheels.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the WIM S video** to see a wearable walking robot.
2. **Read WIRobotics' Series B news** (Korean; use a browser translator).
3. **Watch the EO Korea documentary** about FuturePlay.
4. **Email communication@futureplay.co** only with a specific speaker or portfolio introduction request.
